**Case Study 4: Computer Graphics—Surface Normal Calculation**

A 3D modeling software creates a triangular surface using points A (1,2,3), B (2,4,5), and C (5,3,9) (all units in pixels). Lighting calculations require the normal vector for this triangle for realistic rendering.

a) Find the normal vector to the triangle’s surface using cross product.

b) Determine the area of the triangle.

c) If a light source vector $\vec{L} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$ shines on the triangle, calculate the cosine of the angle between the normal and the light source.
explanation:
a) $\overrightarrow{AB} = (2-1)\hat{i} + (4-2)\hat{j} + (5-3)\hat{k} = 1\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

$\overrightarrow{AC} = (5-1)\hat{i} + (3-2)\hat{j} + (9-3)\hat{k} = 4\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$

Normal vector $\vec{N} = \overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AC}$

$=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 6 \end{array}\right|$

$= \hat{i}(2\cdot6-2\cdot1)-\hat{j}(1\cdot6-2\cdot4)+\hat{k}(1\cdot1-2\cdot4)$

$= \hat{i}(12-2)-\hat{j}(6-8)+\hat{k}(1-8)$

$= 10\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$

b) Area of triangle:

$|\vec{N}| = \sqrt{10^2 + 2^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{100+4+49} = \sqrt{153}$

Area $= \frac{1}{2}|\vec{N}| = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{153}$ pixels²

c) Cosine of angle between $\vec{N}$ and $\vec{L}$:

$\vec{N} \cdot \vec{L} = (10)(2) + (2)(4) + (-7)(7) = 20 + 8 - 49 = -21$

$|\vec{N}| = \sqrt{153}$

$|\vec{L}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16 + 49} = \sqrt{69}$

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{-21}{\sqrt{153}\sqrt{69}}$
